issues.summary: Minor lint issues; also prints nothing on success, relying only on exit code.

issues.evidence: P21_malformed_subschema_no_traceback: properties {"a":"string"} -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' (B/config_validator.py:62)
issues.summary: A non-object subschema crashes with an uncaught traceback; the catch in main only covers ValueError/re.error/TypeError.
Enum check uses Python 'in', so true matches 1 (and false matches 0).
Minor lint issues (long lines, percent formatting, complex validate function).

blinding_guess.why: A ships a unit test suite and handles bool/int enum edge cases with care, which may hint at a more process-driven approach, but the evidence is weak.

notes: Both implementations are compact, stdlib-only single files with the same message format, and both pass all core requirement probes (types, enum, min/max, lengths, pattern, dot paths, reporting all errors). The differences are in edge cases: B lets true match an enum of [1], and it crashes on non-object subschemas. A crashes on non-numeric min/max values in the schema. B adds array 'items' and 'null' support, which was not requested but does no harm, and it prints a summary line. Bandit reported nothing for either side; A's 9 unittest tests pass (pytest is not installed, so I ran them with unittest).
